title: Standardize Embedding Norm Semantics and Distance API for Reranker
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem statement:
Current reranking and embeddings pipelines have ambiguous semantics around normalization and distance metric. Some components assume embeddings are L2-normalized and therefore use dot product as an efficient equivalent to cosine similarity; others compute cosine explicitly. This mismatch causes a) subtle quality regressions for customers who store raw (unnormalized) vectors, b) incorrect ranking when vector magnitudes carry semantic meaning (e.g., model output scale differences), and c) uncertainty when we change inferencing behavior or release new models.

Goals:
- Make the metric semantics explicit and consistent across: embedding generation responses, storage/indexing, DB-level similarity queries, and the reranking service.
- Preserve backward compatibility for existing customers for a deprecation window, while defaulting new clients to the safer canonical behavior.
- Minimize latency/regression risk and document migration patterns for vector stores and SDKs.

Technical background and constraints:
- Cosine(a,b) == dot(normalize(a), normalize(b)). If vectors are normalized on write or read, dot is fine; otherwise dot score will be magnitude-sensitive.
- Quantized/8-bit embeddings (we use q4_* formats) store compressed components; normalization across quantized vectors can be lossy and expensive at query time. Storing pre-normalized vectors or storing norms separately are both viable approaches.
- Many customers use third-party vector DBs (FAISS/HNSW/ScaNN): index building expects consistent semantics. Changing normalization without reindexing breaks recall.
- Reranker accepts batched candidate lists and re-scores using an internal scorer. This scorer currently assumes normalization in some code paths and not in others (exploratory bug found in scorer/metric.go).
acceptance_criteria: API: embeddings/generate and embeddings/bulk return an explicit "vector_metric" field (values: raw, l2_normalized) and optional "norm" field when applicable.
Reranker: endpoint accepts optional query param/JSON field "distance_metric" with values 'cosine'|'dot'|'l2' and defaults to 'cosine' for new clients.
Backward compat: if client supplies "X-Redwood-Embedding-Semantics: legacy", behavior matches historical dot-on-raw behavior for 90 days; produce deprecation warning header.
Storage: database schema accepts storing either 'vectors_normalized' or 'vector_norm' sidecar column. Migration scripts to convert a sampled customer space succeed under canary without data loss.

Tests: unit coverage for scorer normalized/unnormalized paths, integration tests against FAISS/HNSW index stubs with both normalized and raw vectors, and e2e QA with synthetic datasets show no quality regression for flagged customers.
Perf: p95 reranking latency with 100 candidates remains within 10% of today on ci/benchmark hardware for unquantized vectors; quantized path documented with expected overheads.
Docs: public docs and SDK changelogs updated plus migration guide published in console docs and onboarding flow.
Monitoring: dashboards created showing metric mismatch rate (new_metric != old_metric) and topN recall delta; alerts for >5% drop in NDCG on canary traffic.
Code review: all PRs merged and rollouts scheduled via canary feature flag.
tasks: SPEC: Draft formal API contract (embeddings response fields and reranker API) - PR to docs repo (doc-PR #112)
IMPLEMENT: Add 'vector_metric' and optional 'norm' to embeddings response in generating service (embedder-service)
STORAGE: Add sidecar column 'vector_norm' and optional boolean 'vectors_normalized' in vector-store schema; write migration tooling
SCORER: Fix scorer/metric.go inconsistent normalization paths and centralize scoring util
SDK: Add helper that respects server-declared metric and can auto-normalize client-side; bump JS/py SDKs
INDEX: Provide reindex helper and small script to pre-normalize vectors for FAISS/HNSW customers
TESTS: Unit + integration + synthetic e2e rerank tests comparing old vs canonical scoring
DOCS: Migration guide, API docs, deprecation timeline in Console and public docs
ROLLOUT: Implement feature flag 'embeddings.canonical_metric' and staged canary plan
MONITORING: Add dashboards & alerts (NDCG, top1_flip_rate, latency_by_metric)
risks: Quantized vectors: pre-normalization may not be exactly reversible and could change search recall when reindexed.
Storage costs: storing extra sidecar norms increases storage footprint for large corpora; cost analysis required.
Third-party vector DBs: customers who use external indexes may need to reindex; poor communication could cause outages.
Latency regression for on-the-fly normalization of large candidate sets; need to cache normalized vectors and consider GPU-accelerated normalization in hot paths.
Backward-compat flag proliferation: too many compatibility flags could increase test matrix complexity.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (spec + review): finalize API contract and internal SDK ergonomics (1 week).
Phase 1 (behind flag): implement canonical scoring util; default server behavior unchanged; enable feature flag for internal canary (2 weeks).
Phase 2 (public canary): enable 'embeddings.canonical_metric' for 5% of traffic and targeted enterprise customers that opt in; collect signal for 7 days.
Phase 3 (wider roll): expand to 25% then 100% for new clients while keeping legacy flag for existing customers; publish migration tooling and reindex helpers.
Phase 4 (deprecation): after 90 days with stable metrics, begin deprecating legacy header and require explicit opt-in for raw-dot semantics in private deployments.
Rollback steps included at each phase; monitoring and automated rollback trigger if top1_flip_rate > 3% on production traffic.
